meta.titre: Commercial Agents: brokers, factors, indents and commission
meta.sous_theme: Types of commercial agent, open and closed indents and commission calculations

sections.contenu_markdown: A trader in Douala wants to import machines from a country she has never visited. She cannot travel there and does not know the suppliers, so she asks someone abroad to buy the goods for her. In another case, a farmer who has no time to look for buyers asks a person who knows the market to find one, and pays a share of the price. These helpers are commercial agents. The GCE Commerce papers ask you to tell the types of agent apart, to explain the orders sent to agents abroad and to work out commission.

items: Imports are goods bought from another country.
A percentage of an amount is found by multiplying the amount by the rate and dividing by 100.
Producers, wholesalers and retailers need contact with buyers and sellers who may be far away.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Who is an agent

A **commercial agent** is a person who acts for another person, the **principal**, in buying or selling goods or in arranging a deal. The goods normally belong to the principal, and the agent is paid a **commission**, usually a **percentage of the value of the goods bought or sold**.

### Types of agent

| Agent | What the agent does | Payment |
|---|---|---|
| Commission agent | Buys or sells goods for the principal | Commission |
| Broker | Brings buyers and sellers together; does not hold the goods | Brokerage |
| Factor | Takes the goods into his possession and sells them for the principal | Factorage |
| Del credere agent | Sells for the principal and guarantees that the buyers will pay | Commission plus an extra del credere commission |
| Auctioneer | Sells goods to the highest bidder at a public sale | Commission |
| Buying (indent) agent abroad | Buys goods in another country for an importer | Commission |

### Indents

An **indent** is an order from an importer to an agent abroad to buy goods. In a **closed indent** the order names the manufacturer or supplier from whom the agent must buy. In an **open indent** the choice of supplier is left to the agent.

### Benefits and limits

An agent gives the principal local knowledge, contacts and time, and the principal pays only when business is done. The principal has less direct control and must trust the agent.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must find the commission or the amount sent to the principal
variantes.contenu_markdown: $\text{Commission} = \frac{\text{rate}}{100} \times \text{value of goods sold}$. The amount sent to the principal is the sales, less the commission, less any expenses the agent paid on the principal's behalf.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks how an agent differs from a trader who buys and sells
variantes.contenu_markdown: An agent works for a principal, does not own the goods and earns commission. A merchant buys goods with his own money, owns them, sells them in his own name and earns profit, but also carries the risk of loss.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a buyer fails to pay for goods sold through an agent
variantes.contenu_markdown: A del credere agent promises the principal that the buyer will pay. If the buyer defaults, the agent bears the loss. In return the agent receives a higher commission than an ordinary agent.

sections.enonce_markdown: A del credere agent sells 150 sacks of dried beans at 28,000 FCFA a sack for a principal. The agent's commission is 4% of sales, with an extra del credere commission of 1.5% of sales (hypothetical rates). The agent paid 90,000 FCFA for transport on the principal's behalf. (a) Calculate the total sales and the total commission. (b) Calculate the amount to send to the principal. (c) A buyer later fails to pay 800,000 FCFA of the sales. State who bears this loss.

etapes.justification: Number of sacks times price per sack.
Commission is a percentage of the value of the sales.
The extra commission is paid for guaranteeing the buyers.

etapes.action: Find the amount for the principal
etapes.justification: Subtract the commission and the expenses paid by the agent from the sales.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Sales are 4,200,000 FCFA, total commission is 231,000 FCFA and the principal receives 3,879,000 FCFA.** If a buyer fails to pay 800,000 FCFA, the **agent** bears the loss, because a del credere agent guarantees that buyers will pay; the principal still receives the full amount of sales less commission and expenses.

items.erreur_markdown: 'The agent owns the goods he sells.'
items.pourquoi_faux: The goods belong to the principal. The agent only acts for the principal and earns commission.
items.correction_markdown: A commission agent sells goods that belong to the principal; a merchant is the one who owns the goods he sells.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A broker takes possession of the goods and stores them.'
items.pourquoi_faux: A broker only brings buyer and seller together. A factor is the agent who holds the goods.
items.correction_markdown: Broker: introduces the parties, does not hold goods, earns brokerage. Factor: holds the goods and sells them.

items.pourquoi_faux: Commission depends on the value of business done, usually as a percentage of the goods bought or sold.
items.correction_markdown: Commission = rate % × value of the goods; a bigger deal gives a bigger commission.

items.erreur_markdown: Mixing up open and closed indents
items.pourquoi_faux: The words refer to the choice of supplier. In a closed indent the supplier is named; in an open indent it is not.
items.correction_markdown: Closed indent: named manufacturer. Open indent: the agent chooses the supplier.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A del credere agent is paid less because he takes less risk.'
items.pourquoi_faux: He takes more risk, since he guarantees the buyers' payment, so he is paid more.
items.correction_markdown: A del credere agent receives an extra commission for guaranteeing that buyers will pay.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the agent described: (a) a person who brings buyers and sellers together but never holds the goods; (b) an agent who guarantees that buyers will pay the principal; (c) an order sent to an agent abroad that leaves the choice of supplier to the agent.

A commission agent sells goods worth 2,400,000 FCFA for a principal at a commission of 5% and pays 35,000 FCFA for transport on the principal's behalf. Calculate the commission and the amount sent to the principal.
items.solution_markdown:
Commission $= \frac{5}{100} \times 2\,400\,000 = 120\,000$ FCFA.

Amount sent $= 2\,400\,000 - 120\,000 - 35\,000 = 2\,245\,000$ FCFA.

**Commission: 120,000 FCFA; amount sent to the principal: 2,245,000 FCFA.**

items.enonce_markdown: A producer offers an agent one of two payment plans. Plan A: commission of 6% of sales. Plan B: a fixed 60,000 FCFA plus 3% of sales. (a) Calculate what each plan pays on sales of 1,800,000 FCFA. (b) State which plan is cheaper for the producer at that level of sales. (c) Find the value of sales at which both plans cost the same. (d) Give one reason why a producer might use an agent rather than sell directly.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Plan A: $6\% \times 1\,800\,000 = 108\,000$ FCFA. Plan B: $60\,000 + 3\% \times 1\,800\,000 = 60\,000 + 54\,000 = 114\,000$ FCFA.

(b) **Plan A is cheaper** by $114\,000 - 108\,000 = 6\,000$ FCFA.

(c) Let sales be $S$. Then $0.06S = 60\,000 + 0.03S$, so $0.03S = 60\,000$ and $S = 2\,000\,000$. Check: 6% of 2,000,000 is 120,000 and 60,000 + 3% of 2,000,000 is 120,000. **Sales of 2,000,000 FCFA.**

(d) Any one: the agent knows the local market and buyers; the producer saves the time and cost of travelling; the producer pays only when sales are made.

items_markdown: A commercial agent acts for a principal and earns commission, normally a percentage of the value of the goods bought or sold; the goods belong to the principal.
Broker: brings the parties together, holds no goods, earns brokerage. Factor: holds the goods and sells them, earns factorage.
A del credere agent guarantees that buyers will pay and receives an extra commission in return.
An indent is an order to an agent abroad to buy goods: a closed indent names the supplier, an open indent leaves the choice to the agent.
Amount sent to the principal = sales - commission - expenses paid by the agent.
Agent versus merchant: the agent does not own the goods and earns commission; the merchant owns the goods and earns profit.
